I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII hostnames/domains when the email encoding was non-unicode.

### Root Cause
When the machine's hostname or `DNS_NAME` contained non-ASCII characters, generating the `Message-ID` header via `make_msgid(domain=DNS_NAME)` produced a non-ASCII `Message-ID`. When setting this header on `SafeMIMEText` with a non-unicode encoding (e.g., `iso-8859-1`), `forbid_multi_line_headers` failed to encode the non-ASCII header value, raising a `UnicodeEncodeError`.

### Changes
1. [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17) in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py): Encoded `socket.getfqdn()` to IDNA punycode (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`) so that cached hostname queries consistently produce ASCII-compatible domain names across mail components (including SMTP connections).
2. [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L258-L265) in [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py): Ensured that any domain value passed to `make_msgid` (including when `DNS_NAME` is patched as a string) is encoded to IDNA punycode before setting the `Message-ID` header.
